prompt:
PLAN 11 | THE LAST COMMAND
DURATION 15 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9
CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_JAMSHID_WORKER}}  {{CHAR_ZAHHAK}}  {{CHAR_GUARDS}}
LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_SAW_BAY}}  {{LOC_BALCONY}}
PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_ZAHHAK_STAFF}}  {{PROP_INDUSTRIAL_SAW}}  {{PROP_RESTRAINTS}}
DIRECTION AND CONTINUITY
Create a 15-second horizontal 16:9 live-action cinematic sequence. Preserve each referenced identity, costume, proportions and rigid handmade mask; mask geometry and eye openings remain fixed. All visible humans wear their referenced masks. Emotion comes from posture, hands, breath and visible eyes. Each listed hard cut changes the physical camera station, lens or viewpoint. Handheld movement follows a possible path and recovers focus on essential action. References anchor design; written lighting controls illumination. Tactile modern Iranian mythological design, analog realism and natural imperfections. NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.
Zahhak remains unhurried and indifferent. Whenever he walks, show the staff planting first, weight transferring onto it, then the weaker leg following in an uneven step. Preserve the reference's weak-leg side. His two single-headed shoulder snakes remain alive, making small independent movements; preserve their attachment and proportions.
LOCATION AND LIGHT
Night. EAST saw bay lit by a hard neutral task lamp. NORTH balcony lit by weak fixed rail lights and cold sea-sky fill. South of the balcony is the hall; the saw bay lies behind and to Zahhak's right. Fixed exposure within each camera station; harbor lamps remain distant and ordinary.
START STATE AND BLOCKING
Jamshid lies on the idle saw carriage with a hip strap secured and right arm free. His head is toward the main hall and balcony. Guard A stands at his left shoulder; B works near the foot-end controls. Zahhak stands just beyond the north balcony threshold, facing the harbor with his back to the room.

PLAN 11 | SHOTS
SHOT 11-01 | 0s–6s | 6 SECONDS
40mm close handheld from the carriage's left head-side. Jamshid turns his eyes toward the balcony and repeats the command: RIGHT hand rises to shoulder height, elbow bent, palm outward, fingers together. Keep the palm upright toward the hall. A continues arranging a restraint beside the carriage; B continues checking the control area. Neither turns toward his hand. Camera keeps drifting with his breath rather than freezing for the gesture.
SHOT 11-02 | 6s–10s | 4 SECONDS
65mm from the same side but one meter nearer the carriage foot, framing the raised hand foreground and mask beyond. Hold the unacknowledged gesture for a beat. His fingers lose tension; the hand lowers to his chest. A then brings the remaining wrist restraint toward his lowered arm. Fear appears as a small bodily realization, not pleading.
SHOT 11-03 | 10s–15s | 5 SECONDS
28mm stable rear three-quarter full figure from inside the balcony doorway. Zahhak takes one final measured step to the rail, staff first and weaker leg following. He settles his weight and watches harbor workers below. His living snakes shift slightly along the shoulders. The camera stays with him as activity behind continues.
END STATE AND EDIT
Jamshid has been abandoned by the camera. His final command received no response. Zahhak stands at the balcony rail, back toward the room; the machine has not yet started.
SOUND
Uneven breath, restraint fabric and routine tool handling remain audible during the command. At the balcony, water and port labor continue. No silence punctuates the failed gesture.
NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.
